current_example.title: Example: Finding the Derivative of an Expression With the Tangent Trigonometric Function

q-47984.name: Question 1
q-47984.worked_solution:
We know that $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$ Applying this formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{3}+\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}) \\  & =\frac{2\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{3}+\frac{3{x}^{2}}{3} \\  & =\frac{2\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{3}+{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-47984.html:
Question 1
?

Find the derivative of y=2sin⁡x3+x33.

a
2cos⁡x+x23
b
−2cos⁡x3+x2
c
2cos⁡x3+x2
d
2cos⁡x3+3x2
e
2cos⁡x−x23
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We know that ddx(sin⁡x)=cos⁡x. Applying this formula, we have

dydx=ddx(2sin⁡x3+x33)=2cos⁡x3+3x23=2cos⁡x3+x2.
q-47984.knowledge_point: Finding the Derivative of an Expression With Sine or Cosine Trigonometric Functions

q-30988.name: Question 2
q-30988.worked_solution:
We know that $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$ Applying this formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}-11) \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}-0 \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Find the derivative of y=sin⁡x2−11.

a
cos⁡x2
b
−cos⁡x2
c
cos⁡x2−11
d
−cos⁡x4
e
−cos⁡x+11
Submit

q-30987.name: Question 3
q-30987.worked_solution:
We know that $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)=-\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$ Applying this formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡x-5{x}^{2}+8) \\  & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡x-5\cdot 2x+0 \\  & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡x-10x.\end{aligned}

Question 3
?

Find f′(x) for f(x)=4cos⁡x−5x2+8.

a
−4sin⁡x−10x
b
−4sin⁡x+5x
c
4sin⁡x−10x
d
4sin⁡x+10x
e
4sin⁡x−5x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We know that ddx(cos⁡x)=−sin⁡x. Applying this formula, we have

f′(x)=ddx(4cos⁡x−5x2+8)=−4sin⁡x−5⋅2x+0=−4sin⁡x−10x.

q-341876.name: Question 4
q-341876.worked_solution:
The instantaneous rate of change when $x=\frac{\pi }{3}$ is given by the value of the derivative ${f}^{′}(x)$ at $x=\frac{\pi }{3}.$ 

First, we compute the derivative, using the fact that $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)={sec}^{2}⁡x$ and $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6x)=6.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6x-\operatorname{tan}⁡x) \\  & =6-{sec}^{2}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=\frac{\pi }{3},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3}) & =6-{sec}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =6-{(\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})})}^{2} \\  & =6-{(\frac{1}{1/2})}^{2} \\  & =6-4 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change is $2.$

Question 4
?
Calculate the instantaneous rate of change of the function f(x)=6x−tan⁡x when x=π3.
f′(π3)=
2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The instantaneous rate of change when x=π3 is given by the value of the derivative f′(x) at x=π3.

First, we compute the derivative, using the fact that ddx(tan⁡x)=sec2⁡x and ddx(6x)=6. We get f′(x)=ddx(6x−tan⁡x)=6−sec2⁡x.

Evaluating at x=π3, we get

f′(π3)=6−sec2⁡(π3)=6−(1cos⁡(π3))2=6−(11/2)2=6−4=2.

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change is 2.

q-341826.name: Question 5
q-341826.worked_solution:
The instantaneous rate of change when $x=0$ is given by the value of the derivative ${f}^{′}(x)$ at $x=0.$ 

First, we compute the derivative, using the fact that $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)={sec}^{2}⁡x$ and $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4x)=4.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4x-\operatorname{tan}⁡x) \\  & =4-{sec}^{2}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(0) & =4-{sec}^{2}⁡(0) \\  & =4-{(\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)})}^{2} \\  & =4-{(\frac{1}{1})}^{2}=4-1 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change is $3.$
